patch.value: GH-1171: restore parses the on-disk item before consulting history, so a zero-byte or corrupted item file with an intact stream cannot be rebuilt

Reproduced on the 2026.9.4 build in a sandbox tracker: create an item, mutate it twice (three history entries, chain verified), then truncate the item file to zero bytes. pm get and pm restore <id> 3 both fail with "TOON input does not have the shape of an item document" and the item stays unrecoverable even though the history stream is a complete JSON-patch log of every version. In src/sdk/lifecycle/restore.ts the subject resolver parses the located item file before readHistoryEntries runs, so the existing absent-file fallback (replay the current document from history) is unreachable in exactly the case it exists for: the file is present but empty or corrupt. GH-1171 hit this after a disk-full event that truncated files mid-write.

Second half from the same report: a NUL-padded tail (the ext4 crash artifact) makes the whole stream unusable. The current diagnostic names the line ("History for <id> contains invalid JSON at line 4") but offers no salvage path, and history-repair declines because the chain up to the last valid entry verifies.

Acceptance: (1) restore treats an unparseable existing item file exactly like an absent one, replays the requested version from history, and reports why the on-disk document was ignored; (2) pm get on an unparseable file refuses with a typed error that names pm restore as the remediation; (3) a history salvage mode truncates an invalid tail to the last hash-verified entry, records an explicit audit entry, and refuses when any valid entry would be dropped (negative control: a corrupted middle entry must never be silently cut); (4) fixtures cover a zero-byte item file and a NUL-padded stream tail on Linux and Windows; (5) the point-in-time reconstruction gate replays the recovered item byte-identically.
